binders: The target is a closed proposition, apart from an implicit universe level used for arbitrary sample-space types; it has no top-level term parameters.
The bounded-variable assertion universally quantifies over every measurable space Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, and every real-valued function X on Ω.
The Gaussian identity and the exponential-measure assertion universally quantify over real λ.

LocalDef002 existentially chooses one real constant C_G before quantifying over all probability spaces, measurable real-valued X, characterization tags i and j, and positive input constants Ki; its output witness Kj may depend on all preceding data.

LocalDef003 independently existentially chooses one real constant C_E before quantifying over all probability spaces, real-valued X, characterization tags, and positive input constants; each output witness may depend on the preceding space, measure, function, tags, and input constant.
The tail, MGF, and moment definitions internally quantify over real thresholds t, transform parameters λ, or real moment orders p as displayed.
The boundedness premise existentially chooses a real pointwise bound, while every quantitative implication existentially chooses a strictly positive output parameter Kj satisfying Kj≤C Ki.
hypotheses: There are no global hypotheses: all four top-level conjuncts are asserted outright.
For the first little-o assertion, μ is a probability measure, X is measurable and pointwise bounded by some real constant in absolute value, ∫X dμ=0, and ∫X² dμ=1.
The exponential-measure non-integrability conclusion assumes λ≥1.
The non-centered Gaussian-scale comparison assumes X is measurable, i and j are both different from the distinguished linear-MGF tag, Ki>0, and the i-property holds at Ki.
The centered Gaussian-scale comparison assumes X is measurable and integrable with mean zero, Ki>0, and the i-property holds at Ki; it permits all five tags.
The four-way exponential-scale comparison assumes Ki>0 and the selected i-property at Ki; measurability and other requirements are contained in that property.
The bridge between exponential-scale moments and the local centered linear MGF is conditional on X being integrable with mean zero, a positive input constant, and the corresponding source property.
conclusions: For every bounded measurable real X of mean zero and second moment one on a probability space, λ↦∫exp(λX)dμ-1-λ∫X dμ-(λ²/2)∫X² dμ is o(λ²) as λ→0.
The function λ↦exp(λ²/2)-(1+λ²/2) is o(λ²) as λ→0.
For every λ≥1, x↦exp(λx) is not integrable with respect to expMeasure 1.

A single C_G≥1 uniformly converts any admissible Gaussian-scale characterization with constant Ki into any permitted target characterization with some 0<Kj≤C_G Ki, excluding the linear-MGF tag without centering and including it under integrability and mean zero.

A separate single C_E≥1 uniformly converts among all four exponential-scale characterizations, and under integrability and mean zero converts in both directions between the moment property and the local centered linear-MGF property, always with a positive output constant bounded by C_E times the input constant.
mathematical_definitions: Write Eμ[f]=∫f dμ. Every named K-property below includes the explicitly stated measurability and positivity requirements; all equivalence assertions place μ on a probability space.
The exponential-tail property E_tail(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, and for all t≥0, μ{|X|≥t}.toReal≤2e^{-t/K}.
The exponential-moment-growth property E_moment(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, X is also almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p≥1, |X|^p is integrable and Eμ[|X|^p]≤(Kp)^p.
The exponential absolute-MGF property E_absMGF(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, and for every 0≤λ≤1/K, e^{λ|X|} is integrable and Eμ[e^{λ|X|}]≤e^{Kλ}.
The exponential one-point property E_point(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, e^{|X|/K} is integrable, and Eμ[e^{|X|/K}]≤2.
The centered local linear-MGF property E_centered(X,K) is: X is measurable and integrable, K>0, Eμ[X]=0, and for every |λ|≤1/K, e^{λX} is integrable and Eμ[e^{λX}]≤e^{K²λ²}.
The Gaussian-tail property G_tail(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, and for every t≥0, μ{|X|≥t}.toReal≤2e^{-t²/K²}.
The Gaussian-moment-growth property G_moment(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, X is also almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p≥1, |X|^p is integrable and Eμ[|X|^p]≤(K√p)^p.
The Gaussian square-window property G_window(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, and for every |λ|≤1/K, e^{λ²X²} is integrable and Eμ[e^{λ²X²}]≤e^{K²λ²}.
The Gaussian square-point property G_point(X,K) is: X is measurable, K>0, e^{X²/K²} is integrable, and Eμ[e^{X²/K²}]≤2.
The Gaussian centered linear-MGF property G_linear(X,K) is: X is measurable and integrable, K>0, Eμ[X]=0, and for every real λ, e^{λX} is integrable and Eμ[e^{λX}]≤e^{K²λ²}.
LocalDef009 indexes exactly E_tail, E_moment, E_absMGF, and E_point. LocalDef012 indexes exactly G_tail, G_moment, G_window, G_point, and G_linear, with G_linear as the distinguished D013 tag.

The two little-o expressions use the neighborhood filter at real zero and comparison function λ↦λ². The named Gaussian measure has mean parameter 0 and nonnegative variance parameter 1; expMeasure 1 is gammaMeasure 1 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: All of the following are asserted simultaneously. First, every pointwise bounded measurable real random variable on a probability space whose mean is zero and whose second raw moment is one has the second-order moment-generating-function expansion E[e^{λX}]=1+λE[X]+(λ²/2)E[X²]+o(λ²) as λ→0; independently, e^{λ²/2}=1+λ²/2+o(λ²); and e^{λx} is not integrable under the unit-parameter exponential measure whenever λ≥1. Second, the real Gaussian measure with mean 0 and variance 1 has exact MGF E[e^{λX}]=e^{λ²/2} for every real λ. Third, there is a universal factor C_G≥1 such that the four non-centered Gaussian-scale conditions—Gaussian tail decay, √p moment growth, square-window exponential moments, and a one-point square-exponential moment—quantitatively imply one another on every probability space, with an output constant at most C_G times the input constant; when X is integrable and mean zero, the same statement includes the fifth, all-real-λ linear-MGF condition. Fourth, there is a possibly different universal factor C_E≥1 such that exponential tail decay, p moment growth, the local absolute-MGF condition, and the one-point exponential-moment condition quantitatively imply one another, and for integrable mean-zero X the moment condition and the local centered linear-MGF condition quantitatively imply each other. Every produced comparison constant is required to be strictly positive.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Each comparison constant C is existentially chosen once and is uniform over every subsequently quantified sample space, probability measure, function, tag, and input constant, but the Gaussian-scale and exponential-scale conjuncts may use different constants.
The proposition gives no value, sharpness, or minimality claim for either universal factor, and it only requires an output parameter Kj≤C Ki, not a two-sided comparison between particular witnesses.
Every conversion is an implication from an assumed source property. If no positive Ki satisfies that property for a given X, that instance is vacuous.
The non-centered clause of LocalDef002 explicitly excludes G_linear as both source and target. The all-five comparison is conditional on explicit measurability, integrability, and mean zero.

The exponential-scale centered bridge directly compares only E_moment with E_centered; equivalence with the other three exponential-scale properties is obtained only by combining this bridge with the separate four-way comparison.

All ambient measures in the equivalence and bounded-variable assertions are probability measures. The standalone property definitions accept arbitrary measures, but the target does not assert their equivalence in that generality.
The bound used in the Taylor assertion is pointwise: there merely exists C with |X(ω)|≤C for every ω. It is not stated as an essential bound, and C is not explicitly required to be positive.
The moment orders p are real numbers with p≥1, and the powers are Real.rpow; they are not restricted to integer moments.
G_window literally controls exp(λ²X²) only for |λ|≤1/K. It is not a linear MGF condition.
E_absMGF uses only 0≤λ≤1/K, whereas E_centered uses both signs with |λ|≤1/K, and G_linear uses every real λ.
The MGF bounds use exp(K²λ²), without a factor 1/2. The tail bounds have the fixed prefactor 2, and the one-point bounds have the fixed upper bound 2.
The exact Gaussian MGF equality does not contain a separate explicit Integrable conjunct, although the displayed integral is asserted equal to a positive finite value.
Tail probabilities are represented by converting the measure value to a real. In the target's probability-measure contexts these values are finite.
The exponential-measure statement includes the boundary λ=1 and asserts non-integrability, not merely divergence of a separately defined improper integral.
The proposition concerns single real-valued functions only; it encodes no independence, sums of variables, conditional expectations, almost-sure equality claims, or optimal constants.
